subject: Re: Encord follow up
text:
Following up: how does a call at 5PM sound to y'all?  I'd be free afterward
as well.

The episodes are attached.  All are from the first part of our
shirt-folding workflow, where we're taking a shirt that's bunched on a
table and getting it to lay flat.  Here are the language annotations to use:

   1. Grab the leftmost and rightmost edges of the t-shirt
   2. Lift the t-shirt in the air, flick the t-shirt out to open it up, and
   place it down on the surface parallel to your arms
   3. The neckline and shoulder seams of the t-shirt are visible. Grab both
   shoulder seams and bring them down on the surface parallel to your arms
   4. Grab and place the base of the shirt away from you so that the
   neckline and shoulder seams are clearly visible
   5. Grab the creased edge of the t-shirt and pull it out to open it up
   6. Grab the edge of the t-shirt and fold it in to reveal any edges that
   have been folded behind the viewable t-shirt

Our current steps to annotate should look as follows:

   - Attach the corresponding language annotation at the timestamp when
   that action has been completed.
   - *Note *that because shirts are not rigid objects, we have to perform
   some of these steps multiple times until they're done according to an
   "exit" condition, especially "Lift the shirt in the air, flick the t-shirt
   out to open it up..."

Best,
Evan

subject: Re: Encord/Bloomfield Follow Up
text:
Hi Alex,

Thanks a lot for the clarification. Regarding my first question, the
documentation says it supports embeddings "for images, image sequences,
image groups, and individual video frames". In our case we are interested
to upload embeddings (and if not possible additional variables) at the
detection level.

We would start using encord for blueberry only, our first annotation task
would be to review 15 datasets containing between 100 and 300 images each.
Blueberries are already segmented, we would like to review the
classification of blueberries into several colors. There are between a few
hundreds and 2k blueberries per image. I can have more accurate figures if
you need.

To come back to the first question, simple feature engineering can validate
around 50% of the blueberries, but we might need to adapt it for some
datasets... I guess we can add additional tags to each detection when
uploading the data, but adding several variables or even an embedding would
be easier.

Best,

Jean
